BURSEVI:v10p254/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254/r1.claim: The day of remembrance explicates the great calamity; each person will see every good and evil deed recorded, though heedlessness and time had made them forget it.
BURSEVI:v10p254/r1.anchor: أي يتذكر فيه كل أحد كائنا من كان ما عمله من خير أو شر بأن يشاهده مدونا في صحيفة أعماله

QASHANI:79:34-41/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r2.claim: People recall their striving from primordial nature through stages and stations until annihilation, and give thanks for what they reached.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r2.anchor: سعيه في الأطوار من مبدأ فطرته إلى فنائه وسلوكه في المقامات والدرجات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r1.claim: Today people are heedless of their actions and mock warnings, but the Day's arrival will restore their senses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r1.anchor: when he is warned of that day, he makes fun of it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r2.claim: When Judgment arrives, man will regain his senses and see what he earned in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r2.anchor: when that day arrives, he will come to his senses and see what he has earned in the Hereafter

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r1.claim: يوم يتذكر may be an appositive of all or part of the preceding clause, or of الطامة الكبرى, with its case explained according to the Kufan analysis of verbal clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r1.anchor: والمراد يوم يتذكر كل أحد ما عمله من خير أو شر بأن يشاهده مدونا في صحيفته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r2.claim: A strained view makes الطامة itself the recollection, since good and evil deeds or the sight of Hell supposedly overpower all worldly pleasure and pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r2.anchor: وتكون الطامة حقيقة التذكر البروز لأن حسن العمل يغلب كل لذة وسواه كل مشقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r3.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r3.claim: Al-Tabarsi treats the phrase as an adverb of جاءت; another analysis makes it an explanatory accusative meaning I mean.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r3.anchor: وقيل ظرف لجاءت وعليه الطبرسي واستظهر أنه منصوب بأعني تفسيرا للطامة الكبرى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r4.claim: A person remembers every good or evil deed by seeing it written in the record, though it had been forgotten through heedlessness, time, tribulation, or sheer quantity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r4.anchor: والمراد يوم يتذكر كل أحد ما عمله من خير أو شر بأن يشاهده مدونا في صحيفته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r5.claim: ما may instead be a verbal noun, referring simply to the person's action.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#3/r5.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما مصدرية أي يتذكر فيه سعيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r2.claim: That day a person remembers all the good and bad deeds done in worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r2.anchor: {يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى} ما عمل في الدنيا من خير وشر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r4.claim: People recall their deeds when they see them written down, having forgotten them through heedlessness or time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r4.anchor: { يوم يتذكر الإنسن ما سعى } بأن يراه مدونا في صحيفته

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes remembering as recalling after forgetting and compares the Day when God reports people's deeds, which they had forgotten.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.anchor: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعاً فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a relative reading of ma: the things or deeds the person strove for.

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows ma to be either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, without choosing between them.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r6.anchor: أما الزمخشري، فقال بهما معاً، دون ترجيح

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.claim: The author prefers the verbal-noun reading as broader: the human will remember his striving, echoing the statement that each person has only what he strove for.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.anchor: والذي نراه أن المصدرة أعم وأولى بالمقام، فيكون المعنى: يوم يتذكر الإنسان مسعاه

NAHHAS:v5p146/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r5.claim: A person remembers his deeds when reading the record and seeing his place.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r5.anchor: أي إذا قرأ كتابه ورأى محله تذكر عمله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r9.claim: The human will recall every good and evil deed in the written record; mentioning remembrance stresses the terror of the coming reckoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r9.anchor: أي عمل كله من خير وشر لأنه يراه في صحيفة أعماله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24/r1.claim: The person will recall everything done, good and evil.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r2.claim: At that time every person recalls all of his good and bad deeds, as another verse says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r2.anchor: حينئذ يتذكر ابن آدم جميع عمله خيره وشره

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r4.claim: When people read their records, they recall their worldly good and evil and recognize that no deed, small or great, was lost.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r4.anchor: يعني: يذكر عند قراءة الكتب ما عمل في الدنيا من خير أو شر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r3.claim: يوم يتذكر is an apposition to إذا جاءت: when people see their recorded deeds, they remember what they had forgotten.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r3.anchor: { يوم يتذكر } بدل من إذا جاءت ، يعني : إذا رأى أعماله مدونة في كتابه تذكرها وكان قد نسيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r4.claim: ما in ما سعى may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r4.anchor: { ما } في { ما سعى } موصولة ، أو مصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:79:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:35/r1.claim: ‘Yawma yatadhakkaru’ may be a substitute for ‘idha’, or an accusative with an omitted verb meaning ‘I mean’; it may also introduce what happens on that day.
SAMIN-DURR:79:35/r1.anchor: يوم يتذكر }: بدل من " إذا " أو منصوب بإضمار فعل، أي: أعني يوم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#13/r1.claim: “The day” is in apposition to the coming calamity; people recall their deeds written in the record, though they had forgotten them. “What he strove for” may be a verbal noun or relative phrase.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#13/r1.anchor: أعماله مدونة فى كتابه تذكرها وكان قد نسيها

QURTUBI-FULL:79:35-36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:35-36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:35-36/r1.claim: On that Day a person remembers all that he did, good or evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:35-36/r1.anchor: أي ما عمل من خير أو شر

RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.claim: Others identify the catastrophe with the time described by the next verses: perhaps the reading of each person's record, or the dispatch of people to Paradise and Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون ذلك الوقت وقت قراءة الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r4.claim: On seeing deeds recorded in the book, people recall actions they had forgotten, as 58:6 says God counted them while they forgot.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r4.anchor: يعني إذا رأى أعماله مدونة في كتابه تذكرها ، وكان قد نسيها

STUDYQURAN:79:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:35/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:35/r1.claim: Everyone will recall good and evil deeds, including deeds forgotten in worldly life, because all were recorded.
STUDYQURAN:79:35/r1.anchor: All people will remember the good and evil that they have done

TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r4.claim: When the calamity comes, people remember their worldly deeds, both good and evil; that is what they pursued.
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r4.anchor: يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما عمل في الدنيا من خير وشر، وذلك سعيه

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r4.claim: “The day the human remembers” is a time phrase describing the arrival of the Calamity, and striving means serious action.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r4.anchor: ظرف لمجيء الطامة الكبرى، والسعي هو العمل بجد

TABRISI:79:45-46/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r3.claim: On that day a person recalls all the good and evil he did.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r3.anchor: يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما عمله من خير أو شر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198/r1.claim: The day on which the human remembers is the day the Great Overwhelming Event arrives.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r1.claim: The human recalls the good and evil deeds performed in worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r1.anchor: أي ما عمل من خير وشر في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r2.claim: He says the human described is the disbeliever.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p198#2/r3.claim: He identifies the human as Abu Jahl.

ELMALILI:79:34-41/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r2.claim: The remembrance of what a person strove for is appositional to the greatest catastrophe: then each recognizes the aims and good or evil pursued, and profit or loss incurred.
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r2.anchor: “Tâmme-i kübrâ”dan bedeldir. Yani o tâmme-i kübrâ, o gün ki insan neye çalışmış olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r2.claim: People will be shown their good and evil deeds, then remember and confess what they had forgotten.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r2.anchor: O gün insanlara dünyada yaptıkları iyilikler de kötülükler de gösterilir; o zaman yapıp da unuttuklarını hatırlar ve itiraf ederler

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r7.claim: ‘The day when the human remembers’ is an inclusive apposition to the clause about the great event, since that day includes the conditions of Resurrection and judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r7.anchor: و { يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى } بدل من جملة { إذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى } بدل اشتمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r8.claim: The person is shown his deeds in his record and acknowledges them; tadhakkur is the reflexive counterpart of reminding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r8.anchor: وتذكر الإنسان ما سعاه : أن يوقف على أعماله في كتابه لأن التذكر مطاوع ذكره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r9.claim: Remembering presupposes prior forgetting, the erasure of known information from memory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r9.anchor: والتذكر يقتضي سبق النسيان وهو انمحاء المعلوم من الحافظة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r10.claim: The person is presented with his deeds and admits them; remembrance stands metonymically for requital, its consequence, as in the command to read one’s book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r10.anchor: إذ ليس المقصود من التذكر إلا أثره ، وهو الجزاء فكني بالتذكر عن الجزاء
